findings.title: A late-paid order can be packed or cancelled before inventory is secured — mark_paid publishes placed before re-reserving
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: an expired order confirmed concurrently with admin work is exposed as fulfillment-ready before stock is held. For a concrete witness, current product stock is 0 (sold to another buyer); mark_paid writes placed, admin cancels and adds 1 stock, then mark_paid's _reserve consumes that 1 and increments sold. Final order is cancelled but its unit has been removed from sellable stock again. Alternatively packing can begin for stock that the later reserve fails to obtain. This violates inventory conservation and exposes paid orders that cannot safely be fulfilled; ordinary UI actions cannot reconcile the lost inventory automatically. This is a source-predicted interleaving, not an executed race.
findings.expected: R-102: "re-reserves the stock when it is still available" or records paid-awaiting-refund when unavailable; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure" and concurrent effects preserve valid work. Only secured stock should become fulfillment-ready, and cancellation must release only stock actually held.
reproduction_steps: Create an unpaid one-unit order, expire/release its reservation, and sell that unit to another buyer.
Complete the original payment late.
While verify/reconcile is between its order update and product reserve, cancel that now-visible Placed order from admin Orders.
Source trace predicts the cancellation restores a unit that mark_paid immediately reserves again despite the terminal cancelled order.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:91-96 first writes status placed, payment.status paid and stock_reserved True; only :99-105 then attempts to reserve expired stock and potentially overwrites the order to cancelled. backend/routes_admin.py:98-102 accepts any paid order; :127-140 can cancel the exposed placed order and unconditionally return its quantities. :79 allows packing a placed order.

findings.title: Shoppers cannot complete prepaid purchases with supplied configuration — Razorpay server credentials are absent
findings.observed: Payments and billing: in a deployment using the supplied configuration without additional runtime payment credentials, every shopper's Pay action receives 503 and no purchase can complete; no alternative payment exists by design. The handler fails safely and the UI preserves the cart, but the essential buying outcome is blocked. Injecting both valid Razorpay credentials into the server environment would change this conclusion; runtime environment values were not inspected or exercised.
findings.expected: Request: "Razorpay" and "only prepayment"; checklist, Payments and billing: "When ... configuration leaves a payment key empty ... file the blocked checkout". Supplying real server credentials must enable the only purchase path; R-013's safe 503 behavior does not implement a configured payment service.
reproduction_steps: Deploy with the supplied backend configuration and no extra payment credentials.
Add groceries, sign in, enter a valid address, and press Pay with Razorpay.
Source predicts 'Online payments are not configured yet' and no completed purchase.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:47-54 reads both required payment credentials only from os.environ and returns 503 if either is empty; core.py:14 loads backend/.env. The supplied backend/.env:1-7 defines database, CORS and Clerk settings but no Razorpay credentials. frontend/src/pages/Checkout.jsx:77 calls this route as the sole payment method.

findings.title: Customers can be charged without an order or refund state appearing — late-payment reconciliation silently skips older abandoned checkouts
findings.surface: Late Razorpay completion; GET /api/orders; abandoned-payment recovery
findings.observed: Payments and billing: if Razorpay captures an abandoned order after its last reconciliation (for example delayed confirmation), then the user creates three newer unpaid attempts, My orders never examines the captured older order. The expiry scan excludes it and there is no webhook/background reconciliation. My orders filters it out as locally unpaid, leaving the customer charged with no fulfillment/refund record or reachable order link. After 48 hours the same omission applies even without newer attempts. Admin viewing the unpaid list also does not reconcile abandoned entries. Recovery requires access to the hidden order id or developer/manual provider investigation; it is not an ordinary in-app recovery. This is conditional source evidence, not an observed provider capture.
findings.expected: R-102 requires late confirmed payments to be recorded as reserved/paid or refund-due; checklist, Third-party integrations: "an accepted asynchronous request is not a finished operation" and delayed dependency outcomes must reach visible status/recovery. Captured money must be reconciled even when a browser closed or newer checkout attempts exist.
reproduction_steps: Start payment A and dismiss it while Razorpay still reports no captured payment; abandon releases its stock.
Let Razorpay confirm/capture A later, without the browser success handler verifying it.
Create and abandon three newer checkouts before visiting My orders (or return more than 48 hours later).
Open My orders and admin Orders: source predicts A stays locally unpaid and absent from the customer's list indefinitely.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:217-218 marks a not-yet-captured dismissed payment abandoned; :128 scans only pending_payment/stock_reserved True, excluding abandoned/expired orders. :224-228 reconciles only three newest unpaid orders from 48 hours. :229-230 returns only locally paid orders. frontend/src/pages/Orders.jsx:35-51 exposes only those returned orders; no webhook route is registered in backend/server.py:29-33 or routes_orders.py.

findings.title: A customer being made a rider can unexpectedly become the only admin — last-admin compensation promotes any request target
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: with two admins concurrently demoting themselves and an already-authorized third request changing customer C to delivery, both demotions can pass the count=2 check and write customer. If C's post-update count runs while both admins are demoted, the unconditional fallback promotes C to admin. The demotion requests can then observe C as the remaining admin and return success. C receives full inventory, customer/order and role-management authority although the approved action granted only delivery. This is a source-predicted race, not an executed privilege escalation.
findings.expected: Request: "everything should be ... secure"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "server-derived authority stays authoritative"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "walk plausible interleavings ... lost/overwritten valid work". Keeping an admin must not unexpectedly grant admin authority to a customer being assigned delivery access.
reproduction_steps: Have exactly two admin accounts and customer C.
In concurrently authorized requests, demote both admins and change C's role to delivery.
Interleave the two demotion writes before C's post-update admin-count check, and C's fallback before the demotion checks.
Source predicts C becomes admin while both intended admins become customers.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_admin.py:294-296 checks the current admin count before a demotion, then :297 performs the change separately. :298-299 restores the request's target to admin whenever the later count is zero, regardless of that target's original or requested role. No serialized guard or original-role condition protects the fallback.

findings.title: A new account can see the previous shopper's saved address — delayed account fetches survive sign-out and overwrite current state
findings.surface: Shared MeProvider across sign-out/sign-in; checkout address prefill
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: a delayed response for account A can resolve after A signs out and account B signs in, replacing B's me state with A's name, email, role and saved address. B can then open checkout and see A's full saved name, phone and delivery address; role links also reflect A until another refresh. Backend object authorization remains separate and is not bypassed by this finding. Shared-browser privacy is lost through the unguarded client response; a reload may recover the correct account but cannot undo disclosure. This is a source-predicted timing condition.
findings.expected: Request: "everything should be ... secure"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Sign-out clears the user's caches/client state"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions". An old user's response must never repopulate account data after sign-out/account switching.
reproduction_steps: In account A, let the initial /me request be slow while the signed-in header is available.
Sign out and sign in as account B in the same SPA.
Allow B's /me response to finish, then the old A response to arrive.
Open checkout with items and no prefilled address: source predicts A's saved delivery details populate B's form.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/context/MeContext.jsx:23-25 unconditionally stores a completed /me response; :14-19 clears on sign-out but neither cancels nor invalidates prior requests. backend/routes_store.py:68-70 includes default_address in /me. frontend/src/pages/Checkout.jsx:55-57 prefills that address from me, and Header.jsx:32-37 uses its role for navigation.

findings.title: Shoppers cannot purchase groceries in the supplied configuration — Razorpay credentials are absent
findings.observed: Third-party integrations / Payments and billing: with the supplied environment and no external process override, every shopper reaching Pay receives 'Online payments are not configured yet' and no order can be placed. The user explicitly disallows offline payment, so there is no supported purchasing alternative. This is a source prediction; runtime-injected nonempty Razorpay credentials would change the configuration conclusion. The safe 503 itself meets R-013.
findings.expected: request: "Razorpay" and "only prepayment"; R-012: "The checkout payment step creates its charge through Razorpay"; checklist, Third-party integrations: "When every configuration source the code reads leaves a required provider value empty or a placeholder, file the blocked feature". A shopper must be able to pay online and place an order.
reproduction_steps: With the supplied environment and no externally injected Razorpay credentials, sign in as a customer.
Add a product, open Checkout and enter a valid delivery address.
Press Pay with Razorpay; the API rejects checkout with 503 instead of opening a payable order.
findings.evidence: backend/.env:1-7 supplies database, CORS and Clerk configuration but no Razorpay credentials. backend/routes_orders.py:44 reads only RAZORPAY_KEY_ID and RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET; :45-46 raises 503 if either is absent; :72 calls this before creating an order. frontend/src/pages/Checkout.jsx:77 initiates that route.

findings.title: Two shoppers can both pay for the last unit — stock is checked before payment but decremented without a reservation or stock guard
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations / Data, persistence and APIs: when configured payments are available and product stock is 1, two customers can each check out qty 1 before either pays. Both confirmations become paid placed orders, while only one unit exists; clamping stock to zero conceals rather than prevents the shortage. One prepaid customer cannot receive the purchased goods and needs manual cancellation/refund. The same flaw allows a single customer to pay an old pending order after stock sells out.
findings.expected: R-038: "Two submissions arriving together must not both pass the stock check for the same last unit"; R-058: "A paid order decrements each product's stock exactly once by its ordered quantity"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "competing reservations must respect capacity". With stock S=1, total committed quantity cannot exceed 1.
reproduction_steps: With working Razorpay configuration, set a product's stock to 1.
Have two customers start separate checkouts for one unit before either completes payment.
Complete both payments and verification.
Both orders are placed and paid although only one unit can be fulfilled.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:63 checks p['stock'] during checkout; :87-94 writes pending_payment without reserving inventory; :116-120 marks the order paid; :123 decrements stock by id alone, then :124 clamps negatives to zero.

findings.title: A paid shopper can lose their order after a callback interruption — payment completion exists only in the browser verify handler
findings.observed: Payments and billing / UI state, navigation and interaction: if payment succeeds but the tab closes, connectivity fails before verify reaches the backend, or its request fails, the charge has happened yet the order remains pending_payment, invisible in My Orders and unavailable to fulfillment. There is no server webhook, status reconciliation, or customer retry-payment/verify control. Retrying Pay starts a new provider order rather than recovering the paid one, risking another charge. Recovery requires operator/provider intervention.
findings.expected: R-084: "After a successful payment ... the order appears in /orders"; checklist, Payments and billing: "paid state follows a verified webhook or server status check"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "a send timing out after delivery must reconcile before retrying". A captured payment must eventually yield one recoverable, visible order even if the browser is interrupted.
reproduction_steps: With working payment configuration, start checkout and complete payment.
Interrupt the browser/network before POST /orders/{id}/verify reaches the server, or encounter a verification request failure.
Reload and open My Orders.
The charged order is omitted; the checkout offers only a new payment rather than recovery.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/Checkout.jsx:83-85 calls verify solely in Razorpay's browser handler; :89-90 only toasts a failed verify. backend/routes_orders.py:100-125 is the only payment confirmation path; :130 filters history to payment.status='paid'. server.py:29-33 includes routers with no Razorpay webhook/reconciliation route; checkout stores pending at routes_orders.py:91-92.

findings.title: Concurrent cancellation restores stock twice or a rider can resurrect a cancelled delivery — transition writes ignore the checked state
findings.surface: Admin Cancel; rider delivery status; order assignment/status APIs
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations / Data, persistence and APIs: two admin tabs cancelling the same placed order can both read placed, both write cancelled and both increment stock, manufacturing saleable inventory. Separately, a rider can read assigned, then an admin cancels/restocks, then the rider's delayed update changes cancelled to out_for_delivery. Paid terminal outcomes and stock no longer agree; the user may be promised/delivered cancelled goods or later buy nonexistent stock. Sequential replay is guarded, but these reachable concurrent requests are not.
findings.expected: R-052: "returns each line's quantity ... exactly once"; R-053: "a step taken out of order ... is refused"; R-049: "not assigned to them ... status and timeline are unchanged"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "conditional/atomic operations ... compensation" must preserve transition invariants.
reproduction_steps: Open the same paid placed order in two admin sessions.
Confirm Cancel in both before either request finishes; both can restore the same stock.
Alternatively, have a rider start delivery while an admin cancels the assigned order.
If the cancellation commits between the rider read and write, the rider overwrites cancelled with out_for_delivery.
findings.evidence: routes_admin.py:112-114 reads/checks state, then :116 updates by {'id': order_id} only; :118-120 independently returns inventory for each request. routes_orders.py:183-187 checks assignment/state before :189 updates by id alone. routes_admin.py:105 assignment also writes by id alone. frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminOrders.jsx:77-87 has no pending-action guard.

findings.title: A paid order can permanently leave inventory unchanged after an interruption — payment commits before non-recoverable stock writes
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs / Payments and billing: if a database error or worker interruption occurs after the paid update but before all inventory writes, the paid order persists with no or partial stock decrement. A retry returns success through the paid short-circuit and never repairs the missing adjustment. The admin may fulfill that order while the shop resells the still-listed stock, causing consequential prepaid shortages. This is a conditional source prediction for that failure boundary.
findings.expected: R-058: "A paid order decrements each product's stock exactly once"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure". Retrying after an interrupted inventory update must finish remaining adjustments, not skip them.
reproduction_steps: With configured payments, pay for an order containing two distinct products.
Encounter worker interruption or database write failure after order payment commit but before the second inventory update.
Retry the verify request or reopen the order.
The order is paid, but the missing stock effect is permanently skipped.
findings.evidence: routes_orders.py:116-120 first commits payment.status='paid'; :121-124 then adjusts each product in separate writes. :106-107 immediately returns on any future verify if payment is already paid; no transaction, effect marker or reconciliation job exists.

findings.title: Two simultaneous role changes can lock the store out of its admin console — last-admin protection is a read-then-write race
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control / Data, persistence and APIs: with exactly two admins, concurrent demotion requests can each count two and both set their targets to customer. The store is then left with no account able to approve riders, manage catalogue or fulfill orders; signing back in does not restore an existing customer's role. Recovery requires out-of-app operator intervention. Scope is the reachable two-admin interleaving, not every role change.
findings.expected: R-050: "demoting the last remaining admin is refused so at least one admin always exists"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Walk plausible interleavings ... conditional/atomic operations". After any two valid administrative changes at least one admin must remain.
reproduction_steps: Have exactly two admin accounts, A and B.
From their concurrent admin sessions demote A and B to Customer before either update commits.
Both requests can pass count_documents==2.
Both accounts now receive 403 on admin operations, with no remaining administrator.
findings.evidence: routes_admin.py:264-266 counts current admins before :267 updates only {'user_id': user_id}; no transaction/shared guard serializes two demotions. AdminUsers.jsx:25-30 permits role updates from multiple sessions. current_member (core.py:110-112) only bootstraps an admin for new/roleless members, not already demoted ones.

findings.title: Editing a price can put an already sold unit back on sale — product saves overwrite live stock with the dialog's stale snapshot
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs / Business logic and calculations: admin opens Edit product at stock 1, then a shopper pays for its final unit (stored stock becomes 0). Admin changes only price and saves; the old stock=1 is sent and overwrites 0. The storefront sells that unit again even though it was already committed to a paid order. Reloading the form before saving is not a reliable or indicated concurrency safeguard; shortages require manual correction/refund.
findings.expected: R-058: "A paid order decrements each product's stock exactly once by its ordered quantity"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: prevent "lost/overwritten valid work" across concurrent operations. A price edit must not undo a sale that occurred after the form was opened.
reproduction_steps: Open Edit product for an item with stock 1.
Before saving, let a shopper pay for one unit and finish verification.
Change only Selling price in the still-open dialog and Save product.
Stock is reset to the stale value 1 and the sold unit becomes purchasable again.
findings.evidence: ProductDialog.jsx:33 snapshots stock when the dialog opens and :46-47 submits it on every save, even a price-only edit. routes_admin.py:167-169 unconditionally $sets the whole submitted ProductIn, including stock. Payment verification separately decrements current stock (routes_orders.py:123), without any shared product version.

findings.title: A late invalid confirmation can hide a paid order and cause a second stock deduction — failure handling overwrites paid state unconditionally
findings.observed: Payments and billing / Data, persistence and APIs: an invalid verify request can read pending, pause, then overwrite failed after a valid verify has paid the same order and decremented stock. The paid shopper's order vanishes from history/fulfillment queries. Replaying the real valid confirmation then sees failed and decrements stock again. This requires concurrent requests for the same owner's order; it does not expose another user's order or permit forged payment success.
findings.expected: R-055: "a bad Razorpay signature fails and leaves the order unpaid, while a valid signature marks it paid once"; R-058: replay does not decrement stock again; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions". Invalid confirmation must not overwrite a concurrently committed valid payment.
reproduction_steps: For an unpaid order, submit an invalid signature verification and a real valid provider confirmation concurrently.
Let both read pending; let valid confirmation commit first, then invalid-signature failure update commit.
The order is now payment failed despite the valid payment and inventory decrement.
Replay the valid confirmation: it can mark paid and decrement inventory a second time.
findings.evidence: routes_orders.py:106 reads an unpaid status once; :112-113 handles invalid signatures by updating {'id': order_id} to payment.status='failed' without a status predicate. A concurrent valid request uses :116-120 to mark paid and :123 decrements inventory. The paid short circuit only applies at the earlier read.

findings.title: Customers get a perpetual spinner instead of order-fetch recovery — detail requests swallow every non-404 failure
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts that a customer opening an order during a network failure or 500 sees only an indefinite loading indicator, with neither explanation nor the promised Retry. Background polling may recover later, or the customer can reload, but cannot explicitly recover on this screen.
findings.expected: R-106: "/orders/:id ... show an explicit error message with a working Retry control when their data fetch fails". A failed initial request must end loading and let the customer retry.
reproduction_steps: Sign in as a customer with an order.
Open its /orders/:id link while the order fetch fails with a network error or 500.
Observe the source-predicted spinner and absence of Try again, even after the request has failed.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/OrderDetail.jsx:44-46 catches a failed GET but only sets state for status 404; :48 polls again every 30 seconds; :53 renders PageLoader whenever order is null. There is no error state or Retry handler.

findings.title: Admins cannot see all low-stock items counted by the dashboard — panel data is truncated to eight without disclosure
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: with nine active products at stock 9, the KPI says nine but the panel lists eight. The ninth product needing replenishment is silently absent. Admins can recover via Manage and manually inspect inventory, but the overview is incomplete.
findings.expected: R-105: "low-stock figure ... equals the number of rows the low-stock panel lists and both equal the number of products whose stored stock is below the threshold". For nine eligible products, both the figure and panel must cover nine (stock < 10).
reproduction_steps: As admin set nine active products to stock 9.
Open the admin overview.
Compare Low stock items with the eight rendered panel rows.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_admin.py:39 filters active products with stock < 10; :40 calls to_list(8); :55 separately count_documents(low_filter). frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminOverview.jsx:18 displays low_stock_count, :46-55 renders only supplied items without a truncation indicator or pagination.

findings.title: Abandoned stock stays unavailable after 15 minutes for storefront visitors — expiry only runs on checkout or admin reads
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: source predicts that closing the browser during payment leaves stock deducted indefinitely until another checkout or an admin data request happens. After 15 minutes, a shopper merely reloading the last-unit product still sees stock 0 and cannot add it. The stored reservation has no independently running expiry. An admin visit or another checkout can recover it, but ordinary browsing cannot.
findings.expected: R-101: "the 15-minute expiry of an unpaid reservation ... return the reserved quantity ... GET /api/products/{id} afterwards shows the pre-checkout stock". After an unpaid last-unit reservation expires, stock should be available to browsing shoppers without an unrelated action.
reproduction_steps: With payments configured, start checkout for the last unit of a product.
Close the browser without dismissing Razorpay, so abandon is never called.
Wait over 15 minutes without other checkouts or admin requests.
Open/reload the product as a shopper; source predicts stock remains 0.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:127-132 defines expiry cleanup; its callers are checkout (:158) and backend/routes_admin.py:63,89,176. backend/routes_store.py:36-60 reads stock without cleanup; backend/server.py:44-48 schedules only index creation and seeds, not expiry.

findings.title: Late-paying shoppers are told their cancelled order was placed successfully — checkout ignores verify's returned status
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: when stock has been sold after expiry, a valid payment returns HTTP 200 with status cancelled, but checkout announces placement and clears the basket. The destination detail does explain cancellation, so the customer can discover the truth there, but receives contradictory success feedback and loses the saved basket needed to shop again.
findings.expected: R-102: "the customer's order screen shows that recorded state"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "labels ... visible feedback ... against the actual operation state". Checkout must communicate paid-but-cancelled/refund-due rather than successful placement and preserve a reasonable recovery path.
reproduction_steps: Keep a Razorpay payment pending beyond reservation expiry.
Have the released stock purchased by another customer.
Complete the original payment so verify records cancelled/refund_due.
Source predicts the placed-success toast and cleared basket before the cancelled detail renders.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:99-105 sets a late-paid unavailable order to cancelled with refund_due; :210-211 returns {ok: True, status: fresh['status']}. frontend/src/pages/Checkout.jsx:85 discards that response and :86-88 clears the basket and toasts 'Payment successful — your order is placed!'.

findings.title: Stock can remain permanently deducted after checkout fails — reservation is not rolled back when order persistence fails
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: if Razorpay order creation succeeds but the order insert fails (for example a transient MongoDB write failure), the user gets an unhandled failure and no usable local order; the reserved quantities have no order/reserved_until record to release. Subsequent expiry or abandon cannot restore them. This is a conditional source prediction; inventory repair requires admin intervention and the user's retry is a new checkout.
findings.expected: R-100 ties reservation to "the moment the order is created"; R-101 requires released unpaid reservations; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure". A checkout that fails to persist must compensate its stock hold or durably record retryable cleanup.
reproduction_steps: Start a configured checkout for one unit.
Let the provider create its order, then let the following local order insert fail.
Retry or wait past 15 minutes: source predicts the first hold has no persisted order and remains deducted.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:160 reserves products before provider creation. The try/except at :167-175 covers only Razorpay creation. The order insert at :177-185 is outside it; expiry at :128 can only find persisted orders.

findings.title: Expired or cancelled stock can be lost forever after a release write fails — cleanup marks the order released before restoring products
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: with a two-product order, a connection/write failure after the first restored product leaves the other product deducted although the order is already terminal and claims no held stock. Neither retry nor future expiry can complete the missing release. The admin/customer receives failure but has no in-app safe retry to repair inventory. This is a source-backed failure-boundary prediction, independent of duplicate requests, which the compare-and-set correctly rejects.
findings.expected: R-101: abandon/expiry "return the reserved quantity ... exactly once"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure". Release progress must be atomic or recoverable so each line is restored once even after interruption.
reproduction_steps: Create an unpaid reservation containing two different products.
Dismiss payment or trigger expiry.
Let restoration of the second product fail after the order's terminal flag and first restoration commit.
Repeat abandon/expiry: source predicts the second quantity is never returned.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:80-85 changes pending_payment/stock_reserved True to expired or abandoned/False, then runs _release, whose per-product writes are :73-75. Later calls cannot match the original claim predicate. backend/routes_admin.py:134-140 similarly commits cancelled before sequential product restores; repeated cancel is refused by :128-129.

findings.title: Two admins setting the same stock quantity silently inflate inventory — absolute edits are replayed as additive deltas
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: two admins both open stock 10, each enters Stock quantity 12 and saves. Each request adds 2, leaving 14 despite both intending to set the same inventory to 12. Sold goods need not exist for the extra units; subsequent checkout can accept phantom inventory. Admins can correct by recounting/re-editing, but receive success with materially misleading stock. Source prediction, not an executed concurrency test.
findings.expected: Checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "concurrent ... paths ... Check ... lost/overwritten valid work" and "edit forms ... save every shown field". For two absolute edits specifying stock 12 from the same version, the result must be 12 or a visible conflict, not 10 + (12−10) + (12−10) = 14.
reproduction_steps: Open the same product (stock 10) in two admin sessions.
In each Edit product dialog enter Stock quantity 12.
Save both; read back inventory, which source predicts will be 14.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/admin/ProductDialog.jsx:79 labels an absolute 'Stock quantity'; frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminProducts.jsx:30 sends expected_stock from the opened product. backend/routes_admin.py:195-197 increments stock by stock - expected_stock without comparing the stored stock or version.

findings.title: Shoppers and admins cannot use either AI feature with supplied configuration — the required model credential is absent
findings.surface: Ask AI; Generate insights; POST /api/ai/chat and /api/admin/ai/insights
findings.observed: Third-party integrations: with the supplied environment file and no additional injected model credential, shoppers and admins receive the configured 503 and neither AI capability reaches a model. Both screens can show the error, so ordinary grocery browsing remains possible, but both requested AI tasks fail. A valid runtime model credential would change this configuration-dependent conclusion; no claim is made about a live provider response.
findings.expected: Request: "Shopping assistant chat; Admin sales insights" and "Claude Sonnet 5.5"; checklist, Third-party integrations: "When every configuration source ... leaves a required provider value empty ... file the blocked feature". Both chosen AI surfaces need configured provider access, not only a visible chat/control.
reproduction_steps: Deploy using supplied configuration without an additional model credential.
Sign in, open Ask AI and send a shopping question.
As admin choose Generate insights; source predicts 503 on both paths.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_ai.py:26-28 reads the sole model credential from os.environ and raises 503 if missing. core.py:14 loads backend/.env; that supplied file:1-7 includes no model credential. Both chat (:104) and insights (:142) call _new_chat.

findings.title: Riders are shown stale assignments as current after refresh failures — errors are discarded once an array has loaded
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: a rider who has loaded deliveries once then presses Refresh during an outage receives no error or pending/success indication; the stale order array remains indistinguishable from current data. This can hide a reassignment or cancellation until a later successful poll. Refresh/reload can recover, but the rider is not warned that the route information is stale.
findings.expected: R-106: "/delivery ... show an explicit error message with a working Retry control when their data fetch fails"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "Resolve ... failure ... against the actual operation state". A refresh failure should visibly distinguish stale assignments from current ones.
reproduction_steps: Open My deliveries and let it load successfully.
Have an admin cancel/reassign an order.
Lose connectivity and press Refresh or wait for the next poll.
Source predicts the old active order remains without any failure message.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/DeliveryDashboard.jsx:54 catches failed fetches but retains any previous array; :74 shows ErrorState only for the string 'error'; :84 invokes this same load on Refresh. Thus successful initial load followed by failed refresh never reaches error/Retry.

findings.title: Shoppers are falsely shown an empty or cleared chat when history operations fail — both errors are silently swallowed
findings.surface: Ask AI history loading and Clear
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: a failed history fetch makes an existing conversation look absent; a failed Clear hides all messages locally although the server retains them, and reload brings them back. A shopper trying to remove personal shopping history has no indication the removal failed. They can retry after recovery, but only after discovering the discrepancy. Predictions are from the error handlers, not runtime observations.
findings.expected: Request: "everything should be clear, secure"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "a failed ... presented as confirmed ... is a defect" and "failed ... preserve input". Failed history loading/clearing must be visibly failed, not represented as an empty or cleared conversation.
reproduction_steps: Use Ask AI to save a conversation.
Reload and open Ask AI while history GET fails: the panel shows new-chat suggestions instead of an error.
Alternatively, with history loaded, let Clear's DELETE fail and press Clear.
Restore connectivity and reload: source predicts the supposedly cleared conversation returns.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ai/ChatBody.jsx:50 swallows history GET errors and :51 sets ready True regardless, displaying empty suggestions. :100 swallows DELETE errors and :101 unconditionally clears displayed messages. backend/routes_ai.py:117-125 actually stores/returns/deletes user history, so a rejected delete does not clear it.

findings.title: A new AI question and reply can disappear after Clear — clearing remains concurrent with sending and wipes later state
findings.surface: Ask AI Clear followed immediately by Send
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: with a delayed Clear request, a shopper can immediately submit a new question. The DELETE completion then removes the newly appended question/assistant bubble; later stream deltas are ignored because no last assistant exists. If DELETE executes after the backend inserted the new question, it can also delete that new history entry. The shopper loses the new conversation/result until reload (and possibly permanently for the question) and must ask again. This is a concrete source-predicted async interleaving.
findings.expected: R-108 preserves "the conversation and any in-flight reply"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "pending controls ... preserve ... intent". Clearing the old conversation must not erase a subsequent new question/reply.
reproduction_steps: Open a saved conversation and press Clear on a slow connection.
Before the DELETE resolves, type a new question and press Send.
Allow Clear to finish before the new streamed response completes.
Source predicts all new messages disappear and further reply deltas are not rendered.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ai/ChatBody.jsx:99-101 awaits a DELETE then empties the entire messages array. It sets no clearing/pending flag; :79 only guards send on busy/ready, and :124-128 leaves send/input usable during deletion. patchLast at :70-74 ignores updates when messages are empty.

findings.title: Keyboard shoppers lose focus behind the fullscreen assistant — the declared modal has no focus containment or restoration
findings.surface: Ask AI modal panel, keyboard Tab/Escape/reopen
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: after the initial input focus, Tab can leave the chat and reach storefront controls behind the fullscreen mobile panel; closing also hides the focused node without restoring a usable trigger, and reopening never moves focus into chat. Keyboard users can activate hidden navigation or must traverse the storefront to reach the dialog again. The chat remains possible with manual refocusing, but the modal keyboard interaction is broken. No browser layout measurement is claimed.
findings.expected: Checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "keyboard focus ... follows the active surface" and "Dialog close ... restores ... focus". A modal assistant must keep keyboard users on visible controls, then restore focus to Ask AI on close/reopen.
reproduction_steps: At a mobile viewport, sign in and open Ask AI with a keyboard.
After history loads, Tab through the chat input/send controls and continue tabbing.
Source predicts focus can move to underlying page controls although the fullscreen modal remains visible.
Close with Escape, then reopen; the existing ChatBody does not refocus its input.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ai/AssistantWidget.jsx:28 declares aria-modal, but :19-26 only installs Escape, with no focus trap, background inerting, or return-focus behavior. :29 makes the panel fullscreen on mobile and hides it on close. ChatBody.jsx:50-52 focuses the input only after initial history load; reopening the retained component does not focus it. SiteLayout.jsx:29-36 leaves header/main/cart controls active outside the panel.

findings.title: Shoppers can receive truncated AI answers labelled complete — stream exhaustion is accepted without the completion event
findings.observed: AI and model features: if the provider iterator yields text but ends without its StreamDone completion event, the backend marks that partial reply complete and saves it. The shopper receives no cutoff indication and sees the truncated answer as final after reload; admin insights use the same helper. Asking again can recover the task, but the existing incomplete advice is misrepresented as complete. This conclusion is conditional on the specified stream event sequence, not a claim about observed model behavior.
findings.expected: Checklist, AI and model features: "Follow ... partial/streamed output, completion, persistence ... interruption"; "persisting a partial generation as final" breaks the completion contract. R-108 preserves an in-flight reply, and inherited R-016/R-078 require its full text, not a silently finalized partial buffer.
reproduction_steps: Send a shopping question or Generate insights.
At the integration boundary, let the stream yield one or more TextDelta events and then end without StreamDone.
Source predicts a synthetic done event and, for chat, persisted partial content with no cutoff warning.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_ai.py:36-41 breaks on StreamDone but does not remember receiving it. After a clean iterator end, :46-52 persists any non-empty accumulated text and emits {done: True}. frontend/src/components/ai/ChatBody.jsx:89-91 treats that done as complete, suppressing its cutoff warning; history at backend/routes_ai.py:108-110 stores the partial content as an ordinary final answer.

findings.title: Admins can lose the orders page after an action succeeds — late mutations call map on the error-state string
findings.surface: /admin/orders action response during failed filtered fetch
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: an admin starts a slow assignment/packing action then changes the status filter or search. If that fetch fails before the action completes, orders is the string 'error'; the completed mutation's state updater calls .map on it and throws during rendering. The admin loses the whole page rather than seeing the Retry view, even though the durable action may have succeeded. Reload recovers state, but causes uncertainty and rework. This is a source-predicted race.
findings.expected: Checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "Resolve ... failure ... against the actual operation state" and "stale work must respect later decisions"; R-106 promises a working admin-order error/Retry state. A late action result must not crash an error or loading view.
reproduction_steps: On admin Orders, initiate a slow Mark packed or rider assignment request.
Change the status filter/search while the action is pending and let the list fetch fail.
Allow the action's successful response to arrive.
Source predicts list.map is not a function and an uncaught React rendering failure.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminOrders.jsx:69-70 replaces orders with 'error' if a filtered fetch fails. :78-84 keeps earlier actions in flight and later calls setOrders(list => list.map(...)) without checking the union state. App.js:25-60 contains no error boundary.

findings.title: Shoppers can retry a purchase already paid after dismissal — checkout announces cancellation without waiting for reconciliation
findings.observed: Payments and billing: if a shopper dismisses while provider capture has completed but before the client success callback, abandon can actually mark the order paid. The UI nevertheless announces Payment cancelled and keeps the full basket ready to pay again. It neither navigates to the existing paid order nor tells the shopper of uncertainty if reconciliation fails. The shopper can safely recover by checking My orders first, but this is not suggested; following the displayed cancellation/retry flow can create and pay a second grocery order. This is conditional source evidence, not an observed double charge.
findings.expected: Checklist, Payments and billing: "charge/order ... once per intent" and "paid state follows ... server status check"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "failed ... presented as confirmed ... is a defect". Dismissal must distinguish a captured payment from a confirmed cancellation and not invite an un-reconciled duplicate purchase.
reproduction_steps: Start a payment and dismiss the modal around asynchronous provider completion, before the success handler runs.
Let abandon's provider lookup return a captured payment.
Read the cancellation toast and retry Pay using the retained basket.
Source predicts a new independent checkout despite the first already paid order.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/Checkout.jsx:97 immediately clears paying; :98 fire-and-forgets abandon and ignores its response/errors; :99 always says payment cancelled/basket saved. backend/routes_orders.py:217 calls reconcile, which :121-123 marks captured payments paid; abandon :219 still returns only ok. Checkout's Pay at :148 is enabled as soon as paying is false.

findings.title: Shoppers cannot browse the full catalogue after 200 products — Shop silently treats a capped response as the complete list
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: with 201 matching active products, Shop shows only 200 and labels that truncated count as the item total. There is no page that reaches the remaining product. Searching a known name or partitioning by categories can recover particular records, but complete discovery requires extra work and knowledge of hidden inventory. The cap is source-proven; no runtime catalogue size is asserted.
findings.expected: Request: "all the grocery items"; R-076: "every matching product exactly once across its pages"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation". A 201-product catalogue must expose all 201 products, not present the first 200 as the whole list.
reproduction_steps: Populate more than 200 active products.
Open All groceries.
Source predicts 200 items and no next page or truncation disclosure.
Search a missing product's known exact name to confirm that it exists but was omitted from browsing.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/Shop.jsx:44 requests limit 200, :69 labels returned array length as item count, and :91-93 renders those rows with no next-page control. backend/routes_store.py:42,52 caps the result and exposes no offset/cursor/total.

findings.title: Admins cannot browse older matching orders after 300 records — the list has a hard cap but no pagination
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: after 300 matching paid orders, older orders disappear from admin browsing. Searching a known order number may retrieve one, but there is no way to review the complete history or discover an old cancellation/refund case by paging. Admins must manually partition searches/filters, and a large single-status population still remains truncated. This is a source-predicted growth boundary, not a measured performance claim.
findings.expected: R-088: "admin order list ... by paging rather than returning everything"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation". With 301 paid orders, an admin must be able to reach the oldest matching order without knowing its number first.
reproduction_steps: Have 301 paid orders matching the same status/filter.
Open All paid orders in admin Orders.
Source predicts only the newest 300 appear with no next page.
Try the same status filter: the oldest order still cannot be reached by paging.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_admin.py:95 returns the first 300 sorted matching orders with no cursor/offset/total. frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminOrders.jsx:95-128 supplies search/filter and renders only the returned array, with no paging control or truncation notice.

findings.title: Applicants can remain customers after being marked approved — approval commits before the role/profile write and cannot be retried
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: if the user-role write fails after the application claim commits, admin sees an error but reloading lists the application as approved while the applicant still has customer access. Repeating Approve returns 409, so the approval workflow cannot repair itself and the rider cannot open deliveries. Admin can manually change the role in Users & roles, but that does not reproduce the missing rider-profile write; this is bounded administrative recovery work, not successful approval. Conditional source prediction, not a simulated database failure.
findings.expected: Request: "They sign up, admin approves"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure". Approval must grant the rider role/profile or remain recoverably pending, rather than permanently consume the approval action first.
reproduction_steps: Submit a pending delivery-partner application.
As admin click Approve.
Let the application update succeed but the subsequent user update fail.
Reload and retry approval: source predicts approved application, customer role, and a 409 on retry.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_admin.py:228-229 atomically changes application pending to approved through _claim_application; :245 commits that claim before :247-248 updates the user role/profile. A failure in that user update is not compensated or retried. _claim_application at :230-233 refuses a second approval because the application is no longer pending.

findings.title: Shoppers are falsely told stocked products are unavailable during outages — detail treats every fetch failure as a missing product
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: shoppers opening an in-stock product during a transient network/server failure are told that product is unavailable. They cannot retry on the page and may abandon an item that is actually purchasable. Reload or returning from Shop after connectivity recovers can restore it, so the impairment is bounded but misleading.
findings.expected: Request: "everything should be clear"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "Resolve ... failure ... against the actual operation state"; R-068 requires failed fetches to show an error rather than a real empty/unavailable result. A service outage should be reported as a loading failure with a usable recovery path, not a claim the product is unavailable.
reproduction_steps: Open an existing in-stock product while its GET request fails with 500 or a network error.
Read the product page's result.
Source predicts 'This product is not available' instead of a fetch error/retry.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/ProductDetail.jsx:28 handles every product GET rejection with setMissing(True); :32-33 displays 'This product is not available' and only Back to shop. There is no distinction for network errors/500 versus actual 404.

findings.title: Admins see a false empty catalogue after inventory fetch failure — error handler replaces products with an empty array
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: when the inventory request fails, an admin sees an apparently empty catalogue and a zero count instead of the store's actual stock. They cannot distinguish outage from lost products or retry in place, creating unnecessary investigation and potential duplicate restocking work. Reload after connectivity returns is a safe recovery, but the displayed zero is false.
findings.expected: R-068: "a failed fetch shows an error rather than an empty table"; request: "everything should be clear". An inventory request failure must not be presented as a real empty store.
reproduction_steps: Open Products as admin while GET /api/admin/products fails.
Inspect the catalogue count and rows.
Source predicts 0 products and an empty table without an error or Retry.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminProducts.jsx:21 catches inventory fetch failures with setProducts([]); :48 converts that to an empty list, :52 reports '0 products in catalog', and :72-86 renders no rows or failure message/retry.

findings.title: Signed-out sessions retain API access until token expiry — backend verifies JWTs but never checks revocation
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: a previously obtained valid bearer token continues to read the owner's profile/orders or act with their role after Clerk sign-out, until its JWT expiry. This creates a bounded stale-access window for a copied token; expiry still applies, and the code does not establish indefinite access. The app cannot enforce the promised next-request logout rejection.
findings.expected: R-034: "A Clerk session token invalidated by sign-out is refused ... with 401"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "next-request rejection of revoked/deleted sessions". Revoked sessions must no longer authorize protected data access.
reproduction_steps: Sign in and retain the session's current bearer token.
Sign out through Clerk.
Before the token expires, request /api/me with that token.
The backend still accepts its signature and returns user data rather than checking the signed-out session.
findings.evidence: clerk_auth.py:115-116 verifies a signature and decodes expiration; :130-131 returns claims['sub'] and session_id without consulting Clerk session status. core.py:107-121 trusts require_user and reads the local member; there is no session revocation lookup.

findings.title: Returning shoppers see obsolete cart prices and stock — restored snapshots are never refreshed in the shared cart
findings.surface: Header cart total, My basket sheet and mobile cart bar after reload
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: add a ₹50 item, let an admin change its price to ₹60 and stock to 0, then reload the storefront. The sheet/header still quote ₹50 and allow increases using old stock. Only /cart independently substitutes current data, so the shopper sees contradictory bills/availability and must rework the basket. Backend pricing prevents charging the obsolete price; the defect is bounded presentation and cart-state impairment.
findings.expected: R-036: "The restored cart's prices and stock come from GET /api/products at page load"; R-005: "displayed total must equal ... backend". The shared restored cart should quote current ₹60 and current availability everywhere.
reproduction_steps: Add a product priced ₹50 with available stock.
As admin change its price to ₹60 and stock to zero.
Reload the shop and open My basket.
Observe old price/stock there, then open Checkout to see different live values.
findings.evidence: CartContext.jsx:9 loads entire localStorage snapshots; :30 saves price and stock; :43-45 totals those snapshots without a product fetch. CartSheet.jsx:37-52 renders those values. Checkout.jsx:25-32 fetches live products only in its own local hook, never updating CartContext.

findings.title: Shoppers and staff mistake failed loads for empty data or lost access — fetch errors are converted to empty or null results
findings.surface: /shop, /orders, /delivery, admin tables, protected role lookup and product detail
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: a network outage, 401/403, or server failure reads as genuine zero products/orders/users/applications for shoppers and staff rather than a failed fetch. A rider can believe they have no jobs; customers cannot distinguish missing purchases from an unavailable API. If only the related rail fails, an otherwise usable product is hidden as unavailable. A failed role lookup tells legitimate staff they lack access. Reload is a possible recovery but no error explains it.
findings.expected: R-030: "Every failed action ... shows a plain-language message naming what went wrong and what to do next"; R-068: "a failed fetch shows an error rather than an empty table". Keep real empty/no-access states separate from request failure and offer retry.
reproduction_steps: Open Shop, My orders, My deliveries or an admin table while its API request fails.
The UI displays its normal zero-results state or blank table rather than a fetch error.
On a product page, let the detail request succeed but the subsequent related-products request fail; the whole detail is replaced with unavailable.
Let /me fail for an admin opening /admin: after loading, the guard presents no access instead of the failed identity lookup.
findings.evidence: Shop.jsx:42 catches into setProducts([]), then :80-84 says 'No items found'. Orders.jsx:15 catches into setOrders([]), then :26 says 'No orders yet'. AdminOrders.jsx:66, DeliveryDashboard.jsx:54, AdminRiders.jsx:22, AdminProducts.jsx:21 and AdminUsers.jsx:18 similarly substitute empty data. ProductDetail.jsx:20-23 treats even a failed related-products fetch as setMissing(true), hiding an already loaded product. MeContext.jsx:23-24 discards a failed /me fetch as null with no error state, so RoleGate.jsx:25 reports no access.

findings.title: Products and older orders become unreachable as the store grows — list APIs silently truncate without pagination
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs / Performance and resource leaks: with 201 active matching products a shopper can never browse the last product; repeated smaller-limit requests always return the same prefix. At 301 paid orders, admins lose access to older orders' assignment/cancellation controls from the list; customer/rider history and totals similarly become incomplete at their caps. Specific known product IDs can still be opened, but omitted IDs are not discoverable via paging. No runtime timing claim is made.
findings.expected: R-076: "every matching product exactly once across its pages"; R-088: "by paging rather than returning everything"; R-099: lists the customer's own orders; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation". All records must remain reachable, with counts for the same population.
reproduction_steps: Grow the active catalogue to 201 products and open All groceries.
Only 200 appear and there is no next page.
Repeat GET /api/products with limit=10 and attempted later page parameters: the same first ten return.
With more than 300 paid orders or 100 customer orders, inspect the corresponding history and try to reach the omitted oldest rows.
findings.evidence: routes_store.py:42 only accepts limit (max 200), :52 returns a capped bare list with no cursor/offset/count. Shop.jsx:41 requests limit 200 with no next-page control. routes_admin.py:83 limits orders to 300; routes_orders.py:131 limits customer history to 100, :178 rider orders to 200, each without paging. DeliveryDashboard.jsx:84 calls a count derived from this slice 'All delivered'.

findings.title: Customers tracking an open order never see delivery progress — order detail fetches only on mount
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: a customer leaves their placed order open while a rider marks it out for delivery and delivered. Its badge, timeline and rider information remain at the initial state indefinitely. Manual browser reload recovers the data, but nothing on this tracking screen signals that it is stale or lets the customer refresh it.
findings.expected: R-054: "it updates after the rider marks the order delivered"; users rely on: "Track my order" (Footer.jsx:33) exposing current delivery progress. The open tracking page should refresh persisted changes or provide an explicit refresh action.
reproduction_steps: Open a customer's order detail while it is assigned.
In the rider dashboard advance it to out for delivery and delivered.
Return to the still-open customer page; the original badge and timeline remain until a full browser reload.
findings.evidence: OrderDetail.jsx:42-44 fetches only when api or id changes; :58 renders status and :60 renders timeline from that one stored response. There is no poll, subscription, visibility refresh or refresh control. Rider updates persist via routes_orders.py:189-190 but no consumer event updates the customer's page.

findings.title: Neither AI surface can answer with the supplied configuration — model key is absent and direct environment lookup raises an unhandled error
findings.surface: Ask AI; Generate insights; POST /api/ai/chat and /api/admin/ai/insights
findings.observed: Third-party integrations / AI and model features: absent an externally injected model key, both requested AI features raise KeyError before calling the provider. The supplied environment cannot generate shopping replies or sales insights, and the missing-key error is an unhandled 500 rather than a deliberate configuration message. Other shopping/admin work remains possible. A nonempty process-level EMERGENT_LLM_KEY override would remove this configuration blocker; provider/model acceptance has not been executed.
findings.expected: R-018: "call ... with the injected key ... a missing key ... comes back as an error the screen can show"; checklist, Third-party integrations: report required provider values absent from all read config sources. Shoppers and admins should receive real AI results when configured and a deliberate readable unconfigured response otherwise.
reproduction_steps: Run with supplied configuration and no externally injected model key.
Sign in and send a question to Ask AI.
As admin press Generate insights.
Both endpoints fail during client construction instead of streaming a reply or returning a readable configuration error.
findings.evidence: routes_ai.py:26 indexes os.environ['EMERGENT_LLM_KEY'] directly. Neither backend/.env:1-7 nor frontend/.env:1-3 supplies it. :97 and :135 construct the chat before entering _stream's try/except (:32-42). server.py has no exception handler for this failure. streamSSE (frontend/src/lib/api.js:27-33) consequently displays a generic failure.

findings.title: Clearing an active AI reply can crash the chat and resurrect erased text — clear neither cancels nor versions the pending stream
findings.surface: Ask AI → Clear chat during streaming
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction / AI and model features: with a configured provider, clear a conversation after its first streamed text but before completion. The next delta tries to read content from an undefined last message inside a React state updater, predicting a render error with no app error boundary. Even if no further delta arrives, the server's on_done reinserts the assistant reply after the clear, so it returns on reload. Users lose a usable chat surface and cannot reliably erase an in-flight reply without waiting/reloading.
findings.expected: R-016: "a clear request empties only that user's history"; R-087: one active stream without duplicated messages; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions". Clearing an active conversation must safely cancel or ignore its pending reply and leave history empty.
reproduction_steps: Send a question to Ask AI with a working provider.
While the reply is streaming, press Clear chat.
Let another delta arrive, or let generation complete, then reload chat.
The next delta targets a nonexistent bubble; the server can also repopulate cleared history with the orphaned reply.
findings.evidence: ChatBody.jsx:108 leaves Clear chat enabled during busy; :87-88 deletes history then setsMessages([]). :76 subsequently calls patchLast; :65 invokes fn(c[c.length-1]) even if the list is empty, and :76 dereferences l.content. routes_ai.py:101-103 saves the still-running assistant response without a clear/version check after :117 deletes messages.

findings.title: Reopening chat permits overlapping replies and extra provider work — closing the panel never releases its stream
findings.surface: Ask AI open/close while generating; streamSSE
findings.observed: Performance and resource leaks / AI and model features: start a long reply, close and reopen chat, then send another question. The old stream remains owned by an unmounted component while a second stream starts, incurring overlapping provider work and independently appending responses into the same history. Late replies can appear out of conversational order on reload. This is bounded by reply duration/provider behavior, not a measured indefinite leak.
findings.expected: R-087: "Opening and closing ... keeps one active stream at a time"; checklist, Performance and resource leaks: "polling ends with its owner" and subscriptions/streams release on interrupted work. Reopening must resume or cancel the existing operation before starting another.
reproduction_steps: Send a question and close the assistant before it finishes.
Immediately reopen Ask AI and send another question.
Both requests remain active because neither close nor unmount aborts the first.
Reload history after both complete to see independently interleaved replies.
findings.evidence: AssistantWidget.jsx:43-44 conditionally mounts Panel; ChatBody.jsx:75 starts streamSSE with no cleanup effect. api.js:22 fetch has no AbortSignal and :35-48 holds the reader until EOF. Closing removes ChatBody and its busy state, so reopening mounts a fresh idle instance while the previous fetch continues; both server requests save replies through routes_ai.py:101-103.

findings.title: Fast filter changes can show the wrong catalogue under the selected category — old fetch responses overwrite newer results
findings.surface: /shop category/search/sort; admin order filters; product navigation
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: select Fruits then Dairy while requests are delayed; if the old Fruits response completes last, the URL/title/category show Dairy but product rows show Fruits indefinitely. Switching sort/search and admin order filters has the same response-order problem. A reload can recover; until then users browse/act on rows under the wrong filter and counts.
findings.expected: R-001: category tiles "open the matching filtered listing"; R-067: URL restores "the same filtered, sorted list"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: destination/object/content must match the initiating reference. The latest filter must own its displayed result.
reproduction_steps: Open Shop and select Fruits & Vegetables.
Before its fetch completes, select Dairy & Bakery.
Let Dairy's response arrive first and Fruits' delayed response arrive second.
The selected category and URL say Dairy but the rows are the older Fruits result.
findings.evidence: Shop.jsx:39-43 starts a request on each category/q/sort change and every response unconditionally setsProducts; no cleanup/generation comparison exists. :50 and :64 derive the heading from current URL params regardless of which request populated rows. ProductDetail.jsx:20-23 and AdminOrders.jsx:65-71 likewise apply stale responses unconditionally.

findings.title: A rejected applicant can retain delivery access after competing reviews — approval and rejection do not atomically claim pending status
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control / Data, persistence and APIs: two admins can both read pending, one approves (granting delivery), and the other commits rejection afterward. The application then says rejected with a note while the account remains delivery and can receive customer addresses/orders. A write failure between approval's two writes can similarly leave a delivery role on a pending application. This contradicts the rejection decision and requires manual role correction.
findings.expected: R-024: "rejecting keeps the role customer and stores the admin's note"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure". One authoritative review must determine both application and role.
reproduction_steps: Open the same pending application in two admin sessions.
Approve it in A while B's rejection has already passed its pending read.
Let B's rejection write finish after A's approval.
GET /me reports role delivery alongside a rejected application; the rider dashboard remains authorized.
findings.evidence: _pending_application reads status at :198-202; approve then writes the role at :215 and application at :216 separately. Reject also reads pending at :222 before writing by id alone at :223-224. Neither write predicates on the previously checked pending state. AdminRiders.jsx:66-67 leaves both review actions available without a busy guard.

findings.title: Different customers can receive the same order reference — short random numbers lack a uniqueness constraint
findings.surface: Checkout-generated public order numbers; admin order-number search
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: two UUIDs with the same eight-character prefix produce the same public MB order reference and both inserts succeed because their full internal ids differ. The namespace is 16^8=4,294,967,296; collisions become appreciable as the store grows (birthday collision probability is about one-half around 77,000 numbers). Admin search and support/customer references become ambiguous. Internal ID-based fulfillment still distinguishes the orders, so this is recoverable reference impairment rather than duplicate charging.
findings.expected: R-075: "Every order receives a distinct order_number ... a unique value enforced by the store"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "store-enforced uniqueness". Distinct logical orders must not share their public reference.
reproduction_steps: Create two orders whose generated number UUIDs share the same first eight hex characters.
Both inserts succeed with different internal ids and identical order_number.
Search that order number in Admin Orders; two different customer orders have the same public reference.
findings.evidence: routes_orders.py:76 constructs order_number as 'MB' plus only the first eight hex characters of a fresh UUID. core.py:47-52 indexes id uniquely but has no order_number unique index or retry on collision. AdminOrders.jsx:114 displays/searches the order by this number; routes_admin.py:82 filters order_number.

findings.title: Empty or interrupted AI output is presented as a finished answer — neither stream endpoint nor consumer validates completion
findings.surface: AI SSE backend and shared client; Ask AI reply completion
findings.observed: AI and model features / UI state, navigation and interaction: if the provider completes with no text, the backend saves an empty assistant message and declares done; chat re-enables sending while its bubble spins forever. If the network stream ends cleanly before the done frame, the client likewise presents partial text as completed without warning. There is no completion/nonempty validation or retry status. These are conditional provider/transport boundary predictions, not observed model outputs.
findings.expected: R-018: errors "never an empty string or a canned reply"; R-078: "ends with the full text"; R-081: "never an empty bubble"; checklist, AI and model features: validate "empty/malformed results, ... interruption" before final presentation/persistence.
reproduction_steps: With a configured AI provider, send a shopping question.
Encounter a provider stream that ends or emits StreamDone without TextDelta text.
The app persists an empty assistant turn and leaves a spinner bubble rather than an error.
Alternatively, encounter HTTP stream EOF after some deltas but before done; the partial answer appears finished.
findings.evidence: routes_ai.py:33-38 stops iteration at StreamDone or iterator exhaustion, then :43-45 saves joined parts and emits done even when no TextDelta arrived. api.js:39-40 treats EOF as success without requiring a done event; ChatBody.jsx:75-78 never tracks done and :30 displays an endless loader for empty content.

findings.title: Sending before history loads can corrupt or crash chat — late history hydration replaces the active reply
findings.surface: Ask AI initial history loading and suggestion buttons
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction / AI and model features: open chat and immediately send a suggestion while history is still fetching. A delayed empty-history response removes the new pair; the next delta reads undefined.content and predicts a React render failure. With existing history it instead appends the new answer onto the previous historical message. Reopening/reloading can recover persisted turns, but the active conversation is lost or corrupted.
findings.expected: R-015: opening chat "streams a reply ... conversation is still there after a reload"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "initial, ... pending ... state" and stale work must preserve the current operation. History hydration must not overwrite a new in-flight turn.
reproduction_steps: Open Ask AI with a delayed /ai/chat/history request.
Immediately click a suggested question.
Let history return after send has appended its blank assistant bubble but before the next streamed delta.
The history response replaces that bubble; subsequent deltas target the wrong or absent last message.
findings.evidence: ChatBody.jsx:48 unconditionally replaces messages with history when its request completes; :40 initializes an empty list with immediately usable suggestions/input (:94-113). send at :71 appends a new user/assistant pair before history is loaded; :65 and :76 then append deltas to whichever last message the history response installed.

findings.title: Indian shoppers' early-morning orders appear on the previous reporting day — daily aggregates use UTC without labelling a different store timezone
findings.surface: Admin Orders today and 7-day chart; rider Delivered today; AI sales data
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: during 00:00–05:29 IST, new orders/deliveries count under the previous UTC day; Orders today can include yesterday evening's work and the seven-day chart allocates Indian early-morning sales to the prior labelled day. Rider Delivered today likewise uses UTC instead of the rider/store day. Lifetime revenue is unaffected; admins/riders get misleading daily reports and AI inherits the same daily figures.
findings.expected: R-060: "Dates follow the store's day boundary"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "date/time semantics ... user's zone ... time-window boundaries". Inferred from the Indian-store benchmark and en-IN UI, a store day is Asia/Kolkata unless another timezone is explicitly labelled. Jan 2 00:15 IST equals Jan 1 18:45 UTC and belongs to Jan 2, not Jan 1.
reproduction_steps: Use the store in India shortly after midnight, e.g. Jan 2 at 00:15 IST.
Place/pay an order and mark a delivery complete.
Inspect Orders today, the dated revenue chart and Delivered today.
The implementation derives Jan 1 from the UTC timestamps rather than Jan 2's Indian calendar day.
findings.evidence: compute_stats uses datetime.now(timezone.utc) (:17), groups dates by the UTC timestamp prefix (:26), and starts today at UTC date (:39). DeliveryDashboard.jsx:75 defines today via new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10), and :84 compares stored UTC prefixes. Normal order displays use local toLocaleString in lib/format.js:7.

findings.title: AI chat leaves keyboard focus behind its fullscreen overlay and can hide its close control — panel bypasses dialog focus and viewport constraints
findings.surface: Ask AI panel, mobile keyboard use and short desktop/tablet windows
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: on mobile, opening chat removes its focused opener but never moves focus into the fullscreen panel; Tab traverses the underlying header/page controls concealed by it, and Escape does not close it. At a supported desktop/tablet width with a short 500px viewport, its 600px height plus 24px bottom offset puts its top at -124px, hiding the title and close control. These are source-derived focus/geometry predictions, not measured browser results. Closing by other input or resizing is recoverable, but keyboard/short-window chat use is materially impaired.
findings.expected: checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "keyboard focus ... follows the active surface" and an overlay preserves "focus/background interaction contract"; "primary content and controls visible". An active fullscreen assistant must move/contain focus and remain closable within the viewport.
reproduction_steps: On a phone-sized screen, open Ask AI using the keyboard and press Tab.
Focus can move through the obscured page rather than into a modal focus scope; press Escape and the panel stays open.
At width at least 768px and height 500px, open Ask AI.
The fixed 600px panel begins above the viewport, including its close control.
findings.evidence: AssistantWidget.jsx:20-21 renders a plain fixed div covering inset-0 on mobile, with no dialog role/aria-modal, focus scope or Escape handler; :30 is the only close action. Unlike cart/admin dialogs, it does not use the Radix dialog primitives. At md it fixes height to 600px with bottom 24px and no max-height.

findings.title: Riders can deliver orders that never passed packing — assignment permits placed orders and tracking fabricates completion of skipped steps
findings.surface: Admin Orders Assign rider; rider delivery progression; customer timeline
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations / UI state, navigation and interaction: an admin assigns a newly placed paid order without marking packed; the rider can immediately start and finish delivery. The customer's timeline paints Packed as completed although it was never recorded. This can dispatch work before goods are prepared and misstates progress; staff can safely recover by ensuring packing manually, but the promised lifecycle is not enforced.
findings.expected: R-053: "An order moves placed, packed, out_for_delivery, delivered ... a step taken out of order ... is refused"; exposed UI promise (AdminOrders.jsx:92): "Assign a rider once packed". Fulfillment must not skip the packing prerequisite or display it as completed without that step.
reproduction_steps: Open a newly placed order in Admin Orders without pressing Mark packed.
Select a rider from Assign rider.
As that rider press Picked up — start delivery, then Mark as delivered.
The order completes without any packed timeline event while customer tracking paints packing complete.
findings.evidence: AdminOrders.jsx:92 says 'Assign a rider once packed', but :17 enables assignment for placed orders. routes_admin.py:96 permits placed and :105 changes it directly to assigned; rider NEXT (routes_orders.py:156) allows assigned→out_for_delivery. OrderStatus.jsx:13,18 sets every earlier FLOW step done, including packed, regardless of actual timeline entries.

findings_minor.title: Shoppers still get a broken product image for valid URLs ending in placeholder.svg — fallback checks the filename rather than the fallback URL
findings_minor.surface: Product listing and product detail image fallback
